facts.stance: outsiders the old houses neither trust nor fear yet — which is exactly why a seller would slip them a hot relic

facts.agenda: keep the contested commodity's true origin buried so the forged seals stacked in their vaults keep their value

facts.trait: tramp-fleet caravans who carry curios between ports and quietly remember which papers are fake
facts.agenda: stay neutral, carry curios for every side, and trade the one thing nobody can forge: an honest memory of where each relic has been

facts.trait: neutral appraisers who certify provenance for a fee — bribable, but the only caste that can read a true chain of custody
facts.agenda: guard the assayer monopoly; a dissident few would read a relic's real chain for the right buyer

facts.trait: ruthless runners who corner the contested commodity by force and salt the market with counterfeits
facts.agenda: own the ghostlight-amber supply outright and flood every rival's vault with fakes until only Melun seals mean anything

facts.trait: obsessive private buyers who pay anything for a relic with a clean story, real or not
facts.agenda: own the single relic with a provably authentic chain — and burn every forgery that cheapens it

facts.desc: the commodity everyone wants a cut of — amber that hums with stored light. Brokers swear it is mined from a dead world; the truth is otherwise.
the mundane salt that greases every certified sale — plentiful, taxed, never worth lying about, and so the one good every faction's books agree on

facts.title: The Syndics broker the first crate of ghostlight-amber
facts.beat: Long before the market existed, a Vossan clan-broker buys a single humming crate from a Khariti caravan and writes the first provenance scroll — naming a dead world as the source. The lie is born in that first signature.

facts.title: The Drift caravans learn where the amber really comes from
facts.beat: Hauling crate after crate, a Khariti navigator notices the amber is always loaded at the same unmarked station, never a mine. The Drift says nothing and starts keeping a private route-log no broker can buy.

facts.title: The Assayers certify the Vossan forgery as authentic
facts.beat: Paid by the Syndics, the Oseni caste stamps the dead-world story with a true assayer seal. From that day the forged origin is legally real, and the only people who can unmake the lie are the ones who made it.

facts.title: The Melun Cartel seizes the unmarked station
facts.beat: Tracing the same loading runs the Drift hid, Melun gunships take the real amber source by force and begin rationing it — pricing every other house out and salting the gap with counterfeit crates.

facts.title: The Rho Collectors pay a fortune for a clean chain
facts.beat: A Rho heir buys what the Assayers swear is the one amber relic with an unbroken, honest provenance — not knowing it sits atop the oldest forgery in the market. The price he pays funds the lie for a generation.

facts.title: A dissident Assayer threatens to read the true chain
facts.beat: One Oseni appraiser, sick of certifying fakes, lets it be known she can reconstruct the relic's real chain of custody — and will, for a buyer brave enough to want the truth. The caste moves to silence her.

facts.title: The Drift quietly sells a copy of the route-log
facts.beat: Smelling the coming war, the Khariti fence one encrypted copy of their honest route-log into the open market. It surfaces on a frontier stall — and suddenly the true origin is a thing that can be bought.

facts.title: The Cartel floods every vault with counterfeits
facts.beat: To make the leaking truth worthless, Melun dumps thousands of perfect forgeries onto the exchange. Now no seal is trusted, every house is exposed, and a single verifiable relic is worth more than a fleet.

facts.title: The deal nobody dares close
facts.beat: Everything converges on one transaction: whoever assembles the relic's true chain — Vossan's first scroll, Oseni's real seal, the Drift's route-log, and the Rho heir's relic — can prove what ghostlight-amber actually is and own the market outright. The Syndics, the Cartel, the Collectors, and the Drift all reach for it at once.

facts.desc: the original provenance scroll for the first amber crate — the oldest document in the market, and the first lie
the assayer's master seal-die that stamped the forgery legitimate; whoever holds it can certify or un-certify any chain
the encrypted caravan route-log recording every real loading run — the one record no broker could forge
the amber relic the Rho heir bought as honest — the physical object whose true chain everyone is fighting to reconstruct
a flawless counterfeit broker-token from the Cartel's flood; comparing it to a real one exposes how the fakes are made
a wax cylinder hidden by the dissident appraiser, on which she reads aloud what the true chain actually is

facts.text: Ghostlight-amber was never mined from any dead world. The Vossan Syndics invented the dead-world story with the very first scroll, and the whole market's value rests on that founding forgery.

The Oseni seal that made the lie legal can also unmake it: the same master die that certified the forgery is the only instrument that can certify the truth. The Cartel knows this, which is why it floods the market — to make any seal meaningless before the real one is used.
The Rho heir's relic is genuine amber — it is the PAPER around it that is forged. The object the Collectors guard is the one true link; its certified story is the lie wrapped around it.

The Khariti route-log names the unmarked station — and what it really is. Ghostlight-amber is not a mineral at all but the slow-cooled residue of a living thing the Drift has been quietly harvesting; the 'source' everyone fights over is alive.

facts.name: Mara Osei-Vance
facts.role: human stall-trader who bought the leaked Khariti route-log off a desperate caravaner
facts.stake: holds the one record that proves the real source; every house wants it and she can only sell it once

facts.name: Dev Haldane
facts.role: rival human broker on Melun's quiet payroll, peddling the Cartel's counterfeits as bargains
facts.stake: wants Mara's log destroyed before the truth craters the value of the fakes he is fencing

facts.name: Sable Ferreira
facts.role: fixer who smuggled out the dissident Assayer's confession cylinder
facts.stake: marked by the Cartel and sold out by Haldane; trades the confession for protection she may not get

facts.name: Quen Arden
facts.role: the Rho heir's estranged agent, holding the clean-chain relic and tempted to sell it honest
facts.stake: can complete the true chain by giving up the relic — but doing so ruins the house that raised him

facts.title: The deal nobody dares close
facts.summary: Four people hold the four links of the relic's true chain. Assemble them and the market breaks open; let one slip and the lie holds another generation.
facts.next_beat: Mara must decide whether to pool the route-log with Sable's confession and Quen's relic — or sell it alone to the highest bidder before Haldane and the Cartel reach her first
